text.tspan: · finished · $3.76 · 72 ideas
Out of 10, higher is better: uniqueness (how few experts would come up with it) · coherence
1. Loss-development triangle for agent runs: find the step lag where the 0.8B's runs go bad, then schedule
context renewal there
(from insurance claims reserving (actuarial science))
uniqueness 7 · coherence 5
Find the step where runs usually go bad, then reset context there.
Build a loss-development triangle from past runs: failures (hallucinated tools, repeats, format breaks)
counted by step and harness version. It shows the step where failures start piling up. At that step the
harness does a 'renewal': it rebuilds context from the ledger and drops the transcript, which targets
context traps.
2. Confusability-optimised handle codebook with soft-decision decoding
(from channel coding / NATO spelling
alphabet)
uniqueness 6 · coherence 6
Pick IDs the model rarely confuses, and snap slips back to valid ones.
First measure which short codes the 0.8B mixes up. Then pick file, tool and answer handles that are as far
apart as possible under that confusion. Soft-decision decoding means reading the token probabilities and
choosing the closest valid code. A hallucinated near-miss tool name maps to the real tool or gets re-asked.
3. Silent passes: withhold confirmation so the model's confidence cannot inflate
(from eyewitness-memory
research)
uniqueness 6 · coherence 6
Stay silent when checks pass, so the model's confidence stays honest.
Silent passes: when a check passes, the harness says nothing. When it fails, it names the exact mismatch.
The harness logs the model's confidence wording before any check so any inflation can be measured. It
compares this against harnesses that say 'verified', aiming at the problem of confident false assumptions.
